rationale: C04 is expressly invoked by date and provision: the child acts “Pursuant to Section 3(d)” of the December 17, 1954 order. C04 section 3(d) creates the precise machinery the memorandum implements—presidential designation of an officer to advise executive agencies about rejecting foreign-origin bids when essential national-security interests require it. The child designates the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization for that role and supplies guidance on when the exception should be used. C10 has a weaker stylistic parallel in requiring a “clear showing,” while C05 contains generic designation language, but neither supplies the memorandum’s substantive mechanism.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Pursuant to Section 3(d) of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], December 17, 1954, you are hereby designated to furnish advice to Executive agencies with respect to the rejection of bids or offers to furnish materials of foreign origin upon the ground that such rejection is necessary to protect essential national security interests.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: To reject any bid or offer for materials of foreign origin if such rejection is necessary to protect essential national-security interests after receiving advice with respect thereto from the President or from any officer of the Government designated by the President to furnish such advice.
shared_material.explanation: The child directly implements C04’s distinctive advisory-and-designation mechanism, retaining its subject, triggering national-security finding, affected agencies, and operative vocabulary.

shared_material.child_excerpt: exceptions under this provision of the Executive Order should be made only upon a clear showing that the payment of a greater differential than the Order provides for is justified by considerations of national security.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The executive agency concerned shall in each instance determine the amount of the differential referred to in subsection (b) of this section...
shared_material.explanation: The child adds implementation guidance tying C04’s national-security exception to the order’s prescribed price differentials.
